title: A Review of Smart Design Based on Interactive Experience in Building Systems
central_proposition: User-centric smart design, specifically incorporating "people-oriented" interactive experiences across the five senses (visual, voice, tactile, cognitive, and emotional), is crucial for achieving sustainable smart buildings that enhance user satisfaction, happiness, and overall quality of life.

concept_definitions.name: Smart building
concept_definitions.definition: the result of the penetration of information technology and control technology into traditional buildings

concept_definitions.name: Interactive experience
concept_definitions.definition: to constantly enrich the user experience of the rich, to achieve the purpose of optimizing the interaction experience, and to build a more practical, easy-to-use, and humanized smart building system

concept_definitions.name: People-oriented approach
concept_definitions.definition: designed to bring users the ultimate interactive experience, focusing on user characteristics and needs

argument_structure: The paper introduces smart buildings and the growing emphasis on user-centric design. It then reviews existing literature by categorizing smart design applications based on five sensory interaction types (visual, voice, tactile, cognitive, emotional). It synthesizes findings within each category, highlighting how user-centered principles are embodied. Finally, it proposes a conceptual model for smart design incorporating these principles and suggests future research directions.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: By designing smart building systems to interact with users through their 'five senses' in a 'people-oriented' manner, the system can better understand and adapt to individual user needs and characteristics. This adaptive interaction reduces cognitive friction, enhances processing fluency, and addresses both physiological and psychological requirements, leading to improved user comfort, satisfaction, emotional well-being, and ultimately, a more sustainable and humanized living environment through continuous feedback loops.

findings.antecedent: User-centric building smart design
findings.consequent: Sustainable life, user satisfaction, happiness, and overall quality of life
findings.mechanism: By focusing on user needs and preferences, smart design can create environments that are more adaptable, comfortable, and supportive of human well-being, leading to long-term positive outcomes.
findings.quote: User-centric building smart design can achieve a sustainable life, and smart technology integration based on smart design can support sustainable development and improve user satisfaction, happiness, and overall quality of life [4].

findings.antecedent: "People-oriented" approach in intelligent design
findings.consequent: Ultimate interactive experience for users
findings.mechanism: Designing with the user's needs, characteristics, and feedback at the forefront ensures that the system's interactions are intuitive, effective, and emotionally resonant, thereby optimizing the user's overall experience.
findings.quote: In intelligent design, researchers focus on the "people-oriented" approach, designed to bring users the ultimate interactive experience.

findings.antecedent: Interaction experience
findings.consequent: Smart design stage of the smart building system
findings.mechanism: The quality of human-computer interaction directly influences the usability, practicality, and humanization of smart building systems, making it a critical consideration during design.
findings.quote: Therefore, the interaction experience plays an important role in the smart design stage of the smart building system.

findings.antecedent: User-centered intelligent design
findings.consequent: Sustainable development of smart buildings (redefined as bringing users a sustainable life)
findings.mechanism: By shifting the focus of sustainability from purely resource conservation to encompassing user well-being and quality of life, intelligent design can create environments that are not only eco-friendly but also human-centric and enduringly beneficial.
findings.quote: User-centered intelligent design can better promote the sustainable development of smart buildings. Sustainability here no longer refers to resource conservation and the green environment, but to bringing users a sustainable life.

findings.antecedent: Five senses (visual, voice, tactile, cognitive, emotional) perception elements
findings.consequent: Entire experience of architectural perception
findings.mechanism: Human perception is inherently multisensory; all sensory inputs interact and influence each other to form a holistic experience of the built environment.
findings.quote: The five senses are interrelated and inseparable, and the mutual influence of each perception element constitutes the entire experience of architectural perception.

findings.antecedent: Starting from the perspective of the "five senses"
findings.consequent: Reflect the "people-oriented" principle, provide more possibilities for smart building design, improve comfort, satisfaction, and sustainability
findings.mechanism: By systematically addressing each sensory channel in design, designers can create a more comprehensive and nuanced user experience that aligns with human perceptual and cognitive processes, leading to enhanced well-being and long-term viability of the building.
findings.quote: Starting from the perspective of the "five senses" can better reflect the “people-oriented” principle, and provide more possibilities for smart building design, thereby improving the comfort, satisfaction, and sustainability of smart buildings.

findings.antecedent: 3D image synthesis method applied to 3D display on control interface of intelligent building system
findings.consequent: Authenticity, user friendliness, visual comfort of interface, user interaction experience
findings.mechanism: Realistic and intuitive visual representations reduce cognitive load and increase engagement, making the system feel more natural and pleasant to use.
findings.quote: the 3D image synthesis method is introduced to apply the 3D display to the control interface of the intelligent building system, so as to enhance the authenticity, user friendliness, and visual comfort of the interface and enhance user interaction experience [10,11].

findings.antecedent: Users participate in building applications configured and managed on iOS platform
findings.consequent: Availability (of the system)
findings.mechanism: Direct user involvement in configuring and managing the system provides immediate feedback on usability and allows for iterative improvements based on real-world interaction patterns.
findings.quote: users participate in building applications that can be configured and managed on the iOS platform, and evaluate their availability [12].

findings.antecedent: Measures such as "staring" to attract users' visual attention
findings.consequent: Efficient communication between human and machine, user satisfaction
findings.mechanism: Directing visual attention ensures that users are focused on the relevant interface elements, facilitating clear information exchange and reducing errors, which contributes to a positive user experience.
findings.quote: measures such as "staring" should be taken to attract users' visual attention, so as to achieve efficient communication between human and machine and improve user satisfaction [13,14].

findings.antecedent: Feedback mechanism of users, conscious optimization model of visual interaction system
findings.consequent: Better human-computer interaction
findings.mechanism: Continuous feedback allows the system to adapt and refine its visual interaction patterns, making it more responsive and intuitive to user needs over time.
findings.quote: Based on the feedback mechanism of users, the conscious optimization model of the visual interaction system is established to support better human-computer interaction [15,16].

findings.antecedent: Remote consultation of visual system, intelligent nursing data, eye movement control of home building system
findings.consequent: Needs of users with special needs (e.g., disabled)
findings.mechanism: Tailoring visual interaction methods to specific user abilities (e.g., eye movement for disabled users) ensures accessibility and functionality, enhancing their independence and quality of life.
findings.quote: Give full consideration to the needs of users, especially for users with special needs, such as the disabled, through remote consultation of the visual system; intelligent nursing data can be provided, and the technology that can control the home building system through eye movement is proposed to give full play to the visual interaction of users [17-19].

findings.antecedent: Users participate in intelligent technology design work, user experience and data collection, user information database
findings.consequent: Visual level of intelligent building system, users' comfort and satisfaction
findings.mechanism: Direct user involvement and data-driven design ensure that the visual interface is optimized for aesthetic appeal, usability, and individual preferences, leading to a more comfortable and satisfying experience.
findings.quote: let users really participate in the work of intelligent technology design, collect user experience and user data, and establish a user information database, which can not only improve the visual level of the intelligent building system, but also improves users' comfort and satisfaction [20-24].

findings.antecedent: Voice interaction
findings.consequent: Control intelligent building system, automation and robustness of intelligent building system
findings.mechanism: Voice commands provide a natural and hands-free way to operate systems, increasing efficiency and reducing the need for manual intervention, while robust recognition ensures reliability.
findings.quote: Voice interaction enables the user to control the intelligent building system by voice so as to realize the automation and robustness of the intelligent building system [25-27].

findings.antecedent: User participation, deep learning, other techniques
findings.consequent: Sensitivity of speech recognition
findings.mechanism: Iterative refinement based on user input and advanced AI techniques improves the accuracy and responsiveness of voice systems, making them more effective and user-friendly.
findings.quote: researchers often take suggestions of user participation and use deep learning and other techniques to continuously optimize the sensitivity of speech recognition [28,29].

findings.antecedent: Voice characteristics of users, inclusive multi-functional intelligent building voice recognition system
findings.consequent: Accuracy of user voice recognition, functions and experiences for users
findings.mechanism: Designing voice systems to accommodate diverse vocal patterns and needs ensures broader accessibility and utility, enhancing the experience for a wider range of users.
findings.quote: Researchers pay attention to the voice characteristics of users, develop an inclusive multi-functional intelligent building voice recognition system, improve the accuracy of user voice recognition, and bring more functions and experiences to users [30-32].

findings.antecedent: Special speech recognition system
findings.consequent: Speech disorders, safety and health in life (for elderly or users with speech defects)
findings.mechanism: Specialized voice recognition technology can compensate for speech impairments, providing critical assistance and enhancing safety for vulnerable populations.
findings.quote: The special speech recognition system developed can help them solve speech disorders and ensure their safety and health in life [33-37].

findings.antecedent: Speech recognition system for long distances
findings.consequent: Voice interaction possible distance limit, user experience in intelligence environment
findings.mechanism: Overcoming distance limitations in voice interaction expands the usability and convenience of smart systems, allowing for more flexible and natural control within larger spaces.
findings.quote: put forward the speech recognition system for long distances, and broke the voice interaction possible distance limit, to improve the user experience in the intelligence environment [38-44].

findings.antecedent: Gesture recognition as main interaction mode in smart building systems
findings.consequent: Optimization of gesture recognition technology
findings.mechanism: As gesture control becomes prevalent, continuous improvement in its accuracy, responsiveness, and semantic richness is essential for intuitive and satisfying user interaction.
findings.quote: When gesture recognition becomes the main interaction mode in smart building systems, designers pay more attention to the optimization of gesture recognition technology... constantly enriching the participation and satisfaction of users in the smart building experience [47-49].

findings.antecedent: Tactile channel (instead of perception channel)
findings.consequent: Frustration brought by visual defects (for blind/visually impaired users)
findings.mechanism: Providing alternative sensory channels for interaction ensures accessibility and reduces the negative emotional and cognitive impact of visual impairments, promoting inclusivity.
findings.quote: from the user's perspective, the tactile channel is used instead of the perception channel to avoid the frustration brought by visual defects. The user-centered development of such a guidance model can effectively realize human-computer interaction and improve the user's satisfaction [50,51].

findings.antecedent: Different cognitive characteristics of users, series of systems and devices
findings.consequent: Needs of users
findings.mechanism: Tailoring cognitive interaction designs to specific user profiles (e.g., age, expertise) ensures that the system is intuitive and easy to use, minimizing cognitive friction.
findings.quote: Based on the different cognitive characteristics of users, in order to give full play to the advantages of cognitive interaction in smart building systems, a series of systems and devices are developed to meet the needs of users [52-55].

findings.antecedent: Interaction interface between user and smart building, design from perspective of information cognition
findings.consequent: User's experience, cognitive friction in using smart home
findings.mechanism: An interface designed to align with human information processing principles reduces the mental effort required to understand and operate the system, leading to a smoother and more satisfying experience.
findings.quote: The interaction interface between the user and the smart building has a high impact on the user's experience. Analyze the cognitive characteristics of different types of users, and design the interaction interface from the perspective of information cognition, so as to reduce the cognitive friction generated by the user in the process of using a smart home, and then improve the user's use experience [56-59].

findings.antecedent: Smart building user interface simulation model, participation and feedback of elderly users, auxiliary system
findings.consequent: Cognitive function of elderly users, harmonious communication of elderly in intelligent environment, human-computer interaction performance
findings.mechanism: Involving elderly users in the design process and providing assistive systems tailored to their cognitive needs can mitigate age-related cognitive decline, fostering independence and ease of use.
findings.quote: In order to supplement the cognitive function of the elderly users, the smart building user interface simulation model is established by the elderly users. Through the participation and feedback of the elderly users, the auxiliary system is proposed to realize the harmonious communication of the elderly in the intelligent environment and improve the performance of human–computer interaction in the intelligent environment [60-65].

findings.antecedent: Building environment
findings.consequent: Psychological and emotional satisfaction
findings.mechanism: Beyond basic functionality, smart buildings can be designed to evoke positive emotions and provide psychological comfort, aligning with users' higher-level needs for well-being.
findings.quote: With the continuous improvement of users' needs, higher requirements are put forward for the building environment to obtain psychological and emotional satisfaction. In recent years, more and more emotional management systems based on emotional interaction have emerged in the smart building environment [66-68].

findings.antecedent: Different emotional needs of different users (emotional acquisition, recognition, interaction), highly interactive and experiential personalized and emotional intelligent device
findings.consequent: Established
findings.mechanism: By analyzing and responding to individual emotional states, smart devices can provide tailored, empathetic interactions that enhance user comfort and well-being.
findings.quote: By analyzing the different emotional needs of different users, including emotional acquisition, emotional recognition, and all stages of emotional interaction, a highly interactive and experiential personalized and emotional intelligent device has been established [69–73].

findings.antecedent: Various emotional perception frameworks and devices, "people-centered" approach
findings.consequent: Emotional communication between elderly and smart building environment
findings.mechanism: Designing systems that specifically address the emotional needs of the elderly, such as loneliness or need for companionship, can foster a sense of connection and well-being.
findings.quote: The focus on the elderly user group is still the focus of emotional interaction. Design various emotional perception frameworks and devices to trigger emotional communication between the elderly and the smart building environment, and give full play to the importance of a “people-centered" approach [74-76].

findings.antecedent: Combination of different interactions (e.g., voice interaction and touchable sense interaction)
findings.consequent: User's requirements for interaction, daily activities in smart building system (especially for users with physical defects)
findings.mechanism: Integrating multiple interaction modalities provides redundancy and flexibility, allowing users to choose the most suitable method for their needs or abilities, enhancing overall usability and accessibility.
findings.quote: The human-computer interaction in smart building is not only the use of a single interaction, but also the combination of different interactions in recent years. Through various combination modes, it can more comprehensively meet the user's requirements for interaction [77-80]... through the combination mode of voice interaction and touchable sense interaction, the operation of the home system can be realized to ensure that such users complete their daily activities in the smart building system [1,81-83].

findings.antecedent: Define the needs (physiological needs, psychological needs)
findings.consequent: Smart building design
findings.mechanism: Understanding fundamental user requirements, both functional and emotional, is the foundational step for designing smart buildings that truly serve human well-being.
findings.quote: Define the needs (Physiological needs, Psychological needs)

findings.antecedent: User participation (test experience, provide advice)
findings.consequent: Smart building forming phase (in progress)
findings.mechanism: Involving users in testing and providing feedback during the development phase allows for iterative design improvements, ensuring the system evolves to meet real-world user expectations and preferences.
findings.quote: User participation (Test experience, Provide advice)

findings.antecedent: User feedback (stability performance, interaction mode, emotional expression)
findings.consequent: Smart building use phase (afterwards)
findings.mechanism: Continuous monitoring of user feedback on system performance, interaction quality, and emotional impact during the use phase enables ongoing optimization and adaptation, ensuring long-term user satisfaction.
findings.quote: User Feedback (Stability performance, Interaction mode, Emotional expression)

findings.antecedent: "People-oriented" interactive experience design principle
findings.consequent: Security, effectiveness, and sustainability of the smart building system
findings.mechanism: By prioritizing human needs and experiences, design ensures that smart buildings are not only technologically advanced but also safe, efficient, and conducive to long-term human well-being and environmental harmony.
findings.quote: First, the principle of "people-oriented" interactive experience design is to ensure the security, effectiveness, and sustainability of the smart building system, including intelligent communication in the building environment, which fundamentally changes the traditional smart building interaction mode.

findings.antecedent: "People-oriented" interactive experience, continuous development of times, more and more attention
findings.consequent: Research of principles of "people-oriented" interactive experience
findings.mechanism: The increasing recognition of the importance of human-centered design, coupled with technological advancements, drives continuous research and development in this area.
findings.quote: In the research of principles of "people-oriented" interactive experience, with the continuous development of the times, more and more attention has been paid.

findings.antecedent: Smart building system, different interaction elements
findings.consequent: Satisfaction degree of people in smart building service
findings.mechanism: The performance and design of the control system, and the specific interaction elements it employs, directly dictate how well user needs are met and how positive their experience is.
findings.source: 2.1. Step 1: Identifying the Research Question, page 3
findings.quote: the performance of the control system also determines the satisfaction degree of the people in the smart building service.

findings.antecedent: Performance of the control system
findings.consequent: Intelligence of the building system
findings.mechanism: The sophistication and effectiveness of the control system, which integrates information technology and automation, directly dictates the overall intelligence and responsiveness of the smart building.
findings.source: 2.1. Step 1: Identifying the Research Question, page 3
findings.quote: the performance of the control system determines the intelligence of the building system.

findings.antecedent: Performance of the control system
findings.consequent: Intelligent technology
findings.mechanism: The capabilities of the control system are directly enabled and limited by the underlying intelligent technologies (e.g., AI, sensors, actuators) that process information and execute commands.
findings.source: 2.1. Step 1: Identifying the Research Question, page 3
findings.quote: The performance of the control system mainly depends on intelligent technology.

findings.antecedent: Interactive experience design principle (based on cognitive psychology, design psychology, related theories)
findings.consequent: Design of smart building technology, human-computer interaction mode
findings.mechanism: By applying principles from cognitive and design psychology, interactive experience design can create more intuitive, efficient, and humanized interfaces, bridging the gap between human and machine.
findings.source: 2.1. Step 1: Identifying the Research Question, page 3
findings.quote: The "people-oriented" interactive experience design principle based on cognitive psychology, design psychology, and other related theories has a significant impact on the design of smart building technology, fully plays the role of interactive experience, builds a bridge between information transmission and the intelligent environment, and achieves a more complete human-computer interaction mode.

findings.antecedent: Smart building system
findings.consequent: Users' needs (physiological, psychological)
findings.mechanism: A well-designed smart building system should address both the functional (physiological) and emotional (psychological) needs of its occupants to provide comprehensive well-being.
findings.quote: Before the development of smart home technology, the needs of users, including physiological needs (functional needs) and psychological needs (emotional needs), will be fully considered.

findings.antecedent: Smart design of the building system (in terms of physiological needs)
findings.consequent: People's quality of life, convenience, comfort
findings.mechanism: By automating tasks, optimizing environmental conditions, and providing assistive functions, smart design directly enhances physical comfort and reduces daily burdens.
findings.quote: In terms of physiological needs, the smart design of the building system has improved people's quality of life to a certain extent, bringing convenience and comfort to people's lives.

findings.antecedent: Smart design of the building system (in terms of psychological needs)
findings.consequent: Information exchange between human and computer, psychological services to users
findings.mechanism: Smart systems can facilitate communication, provide emotional support, and adapt to user moods, thereby addressing psychological needs and enhancing mental well-being.
findings.quote: In terms of psychological needs, the smart design of the building system enables information exchange between human and computer, and improves psychological services to users.

findings.antecedent: Application of interactive experience
findings.consequent: Users' needs
findings.mechanism: Effective interactive design ensures that the system responds to and anticipates user needs, leading to a sense of control, personalization, and overall satisfaction.
findings.quote: Therefore, it is extremely important to satisfy users' needs in the application of interactive experience.

findings.antecedent: Principle of reasonable use of time, space, and family members (in interactive experience technology)
findings.consequent: Whole family benefit from smart design of the building system
findings.mechanism: Thoughtful planning ensures that smart systems are integrated in a way that optimizes resource allocation and supports the needs of all family members, preventing conflicts and maximizing collective well-being.
findings.quote: In the application of interactive experience technology, we should follow the principle of the reasonable use of time, space, and family members, so that the whole family can benefit from the smart design of the building system.

findings.antecedent: Users participate in early design stage of smart buildings, provide reasonable requirements
findings.consequent: Basic model for interactive experience of smart building systems
findings.mechanism: Early user involvement ensures that the foundational design principles and models are aligned with real-world needs and preferences, creating a robust basis for future development.
findings.quote: From the perspective of cognitive psychology, let users participate in the early design stage of smart buildings, put forward reasonable requirements, and provide a basic model for the interactive experience of the smart building systems.

findings.antecedent: User's real reaction
findings.consequent: Degree of acceptance of the smart building system
findings.mechanism: The ultimate success of a smart building system hinges on how users actually perceive and interact with it, making their real-time responses a critical indicator of design effectiveness.
findings.quote: in the smart building system, the user's real reaction determines the degree of acceptance of the smart building system.

findings.antecedent: Product technology characteristics (stability performance, interaction mode, emotional expression)
findings.consequent: User's feelings
findings.mechanism: The technical attributes of the smart system directly influence the user's emotional and cognitive responses, determining whether the experience is positive or negative.
findings.quote: The user's feelings mainly depend on the following characteristics of product technology—stability performance, interaction mode, emotional expression, and so on [78,83].

findings.antecedent: Smart building system
findings.consequent: Certain stability, all kinds of smart designs perform duties, adapt to more use environments, stable performance of smart environment
findings.mechanism: A reliable and consistent system ensures that all functionalities operate as intended across various conditions, building user trust and preventing frustration.
findings.quote: Therefore, the smart building system should have a certain stability, and no matter how much user participation, all kinds of smart designs can perform their duties, adapt to more use environments, and ensure the stable performance of the smart environment.

findings.antecedent: Good human-computer interaction mode, smart building environment that can be exchanged, human emotions
findings.consequent: Building is no longer a cold space, emotional changes of users, home environment adjusted according to changes, mood of users, users' close friends
findings.mechanism: By designing for empathetic and responsive interactions, smart buildings can become dynamic, emotionally intelligent spaces that adapt to and support human well-being, fostering a sense of connection and comfort.
findings.quote: It should have a good human-computer interaction mode, and create a smart building environment that can be exchanged, so that the building is no longer a cold space; it should have human emotions, feel the emotional changes of users at all times, and adjust the home environment according to the changes, alleviate the mood of users, and be users' close friends.

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: Empirical studies could test the impact of 'five senses' interactive design on user satisfaction, comfort, and physiological/psychological well-being in smart buildings.

Future research should focus on how to realize the humanization of smart buildings and effective communication between people, promoting a more intelligent, human-oriented, and personalized direction for smart building systems.
The development of 5G smart buildings will receive more attention and offers opportunities for enhanced efficiency, rapidity, and economy in interactive experiences.
bridge_warrants: The paper explicitly links 'people-oriented' design to sustainability, broadening the traditional definition of sustainability beyond resource conservation to encompass user well-being and quality of life.
It connects interactive experience design principles to cognitive psychology and design psychology, providing a theoretical basis for human-computer interaction in smart environments.
methodological_critiques: Few existing studies start from the perspective of interactive experience and use the 'five senses' interaction type to prove the importance of the 'people-oriented' approach in smart design, indicating a research gap.
model_structure: The paper proposes two conceptual models. Figure 1 illustrates a 'Basic model diagram of a smart building system' comprising a 'Person', 'Smart Building Control System', and 'Electronic Product', with mutual 'information transfer' and 'information feedback'. 'Smart Design' influences the control system, which mediates 'five senses' interactions (visual, audible, sensible, touchable, emotional) between the person and electronic product. Figure 4 presents an 'Application of interactive experience in smart design of the building system' model, outlining three phases: 'Define the needs' (physiological, psychological), 'User participation' (test experience, advice), and 'User Feedback' (stability, interaction mode, emotional expression), which correspond to the 'Smart Building Design Phase (beforehand)', 'Smart Building Forming Phase (in progress)', and 'Smart Building Use Phase (afterwards)', respectively, with feedback loops between phases.
limitations: The paper, as a review, relies on existing literature and may be subject to inherent biases of published research.
The practical implementation of complex interactive combinations in smart buildings faces technological challenges.

User-centric building smart design can achieve a sustainable life, and smart technology integration based on smart design can support sustainable development and improve user satisfaction, happiness, and overall quality of life. In intelligent design, researchers focus on the “people-oriented” approach, designed to bring users the ultimate interactive experience. Based on the interactive experience principle of smart design in the smart building system, this article classifies and summarizes intelligent design from the “five senses” interaction, including visual interaction, voice interaction, tactile interaction, cognitive interaction, and emotional interaction. We analyze the application of smart design in architecture and discuss how to embody the principles of user-centered interactive experience design in the process of smart design. This article provides a comprehensive and systematic literature review, clarifies the importance of the “people-oriented” approach in the smart design of buildings, and summarizes how to improve the sustainability of intelligent buildings from the perspective of a “people-oriented” approach. This paper proposes future research suggestions and directions and promotes the sustainable development of the smart building.
